title: Heats of Reactions Can Be Calculated from Tabulated Heats of Formation
lead: No table could list the enthalpy of every reaction. Chemists tabulate a few kinds instead: forming a compound from its elements in their standard states, adding or removing an electron, and breaking a bond in the gas.
exercise_notes: The book prints no exercises here; both questions and their solutions were written by AI. Numeric answers accept a 2% tolerance.

ai.part: kept as the book prints it

exercises.prompt: Propane burns by C3H8(g) + 5O2(g) → 3CO2(g) + 4H2O(l). Find $\kDeltaHrxn$ at 25 °C for the reaction as written from the standard enthalpies of formation in this section: C3H8(g) −103.8, CO2(g) −393.5 and H2O(l) −285.8 kJ/mol.

answer.hint: O₂ is an element in its standard state, so its $\kDeltaHf$ is zero.
answer.solution: The products contribute $3(-393.5) + 4(-285.8) = -1180.5 - 1143.2 = -2323.7$ kJ and the reactants $1(-103.8) + 5(0) = -103.8$ kJ, since O2(g) is an element in its standard state. Then $\kDeltaHrxn = -2323.7 - (-103.8) = -2219.9$ kJ: burning one mole of propane with five moles of oxygen releases 2219.9 kJ at 25 °C.

exercises.prompt: Estimate $\kDeltaHrxn$ for CH4(g) + 2O2(g) → CO2(g) + 2H2O(g) from the average bond energies in the table.

answer.hint: Count the bonds: CH₄ has four C–H, each O₂ one O=O, CO₂ two C=O and each H₂O two O–H.
answer.solution: Broken: four C–H and two O=O, $4(413) + 2(495) = 1652 + 990 = 2642$ kJ. Formed: two C=O and four O–H, $2(799) + 4(463) = 1598 + 1852 = 3450$ kJ. So $\kDeltaHrxn \approx 2642 - 3450 = -808$ kJ. The water is a gas here, as the bond energies assume; the tabulated value for liquid water, −890.5 kJ, also includes the heat of condensation.

footnotes.html: The two bracketed reactions should read $CO(g) \rightarrow C(gr) + \tfrac{1}{2}O_2(g)$, the first data reaction reversed, and $C(gr) + O_2(g) \rightarrow CO_2(g)$, the second as given. Twice each of these adds up to the target reaction; the lines as printed do not.
The labels are swapped: $-787.02$ kJ is $2\Delta H_2$, and $+221.06$ kJ is $-2\Delta H_1$, twice the reversed first reaction. The total, $-565.96$ kJ, is right.

The scheme is not balanced, and the sum in Equation 19.12.2 counts two O–H bonds formed. Balanced, C<sub>2</sub>H<sub>5</sub>OH + 3O<sub>2</sub> → 2CO<sub>2</sub> + 3H<sub>2</sub>O breaks five C–H, one C–C, one C–O, one O–H and three O=O bonds and forms four C=O and six O–H bonds, so the table gives $\kDeltaHc \approx 4719 - 5974 = -1255$ kJ/mol.
